text:
alex: heads-up — I reproduced steady memory growth on long streaming/tool-loop runs after the kernel-selection change (PR #814). Heap climbs ~30MB/hr on a 12h session.

priya: ugh. is this during tool-heavy loops or normal chat streaming?

alex: tool-heavy. pattern: repeated tool call -> append to kv -> next step reuses kv but memory doesn't free. repro script attached.

mike: can you paste the pmap / top output from the failing worker?

alex: pasted minimal logs below:
```
PID  /proc/12345/status
VmRSS:  210000 kB
... after 1h
VmRSS:  245000 kB
... after 6h
VmRSS:  410000 kB
```
Also heaptrack snapshots show steady growth in `KvPage::append` and `SlabAllocator::alloc_chunk`.

sarah: interesting — kernel selection switch favored the AVX512 fused-kernel path for attention which changed scheduling and batching behavior. could that change the kv page churn?

priya: PROFILE: ran `perf script` + flamegraph. Main alloc sites point to page coalescer and `vec::resize` in the page index. Not direct leak but retention.

alex: exact flame snippet: `kv::page_coalescer::merge_ranges` -> `kv::PageIndex::insert` -> `Vec<T>::push` (growing) repeated per tool result.

mike: does GC/eviction not trigger because of pinned refs? check holdcount traces.

alex: yes — holdcount shows a long-lived pin during streaming: each token append briefly increments a pin, but a race keeps the global `SessionHold` alive across tool boundaries. suspect: batching heuristic changed request grouping so the final release deferred.

priya: steps I tried: force-evict at route boundary, turned off reuse caching, ran with older kernel path — memory stable. So it's in the interaction between reused KV windows + new kernel scheduling.

mike: can you share the exact repro command? I'll run with jemalloc profiling on a dedicated host.

alex: repro (short):
```
./run_streaming_test --session-length 50000 --tool-calls 120 --batching=continuous --kernel=auto
# watch rss
```
I also have a branch with an injected `tracepoint` in `Session::release` that rarely never fires.

infra-bot: ci/bench/streaming-longrun completed: 50% pass, memory regression +18% over baseline.

sarah: next plan: mike will run jemalloc + heaptrack with the new kernel path; priya will audit holdcount refs and add assert checks on release paths; alex will keep the repro harness and provide traces.

mike: on it. I suspect the kernel path increased a small window where `KVCache::try_reuse` returns true but ownership isn't transferred; that leads to orphaned page chains until a compaction runs. Will instrument `try_reuse` and `Page::owner` transitions.

priya: I'll add assertion in staging for ephemeral builds to detect >10s pin lifetimes and fail fast. Also add a TTL-based fallback to force eviction.

alex: thanks. tagging follow-ups: add a quick triage doc in the bug board and assign to eng-runtime for the week. If anyone hits the repro, ping me and I can hand off the harness.

mike: will post results here when I have jemalloc dumps (ETA ~4h).

sarah: if this is a timing/regression introduced by kernel scheduling, we might need to revert until fix is up; but let's wait for the dumps.

alex: agreed. temporary mitigation: set `kernel.selection=legacy` for hot pools. I'll prototype a rollout toggle.

priya: noted — I'll prepare an alert to surface >10% mem delta for streaming pools so we catch this earlier.

mike: jemalloc profile started. will share `jeprof` and `heaptrack` output here.

alex: thanks all — good triage.
